root_cause.text: In the krealloc and kvrealloc fallback paths, the memcpy copy length was not bounded by the new allocation size, and in __do_krealloc() the old size variables (ks, orig_size) were uninitialized when an early jump to the fallback path occurred due to NUMA node mismatch, causing either zero-byte copy (data loss) or out-of-bounds write when shrinking.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly identifies two bugs: (1) "The jump to 'alloc_new' happens before 'ks' and 'orig_size' are initialized. As a result, the memcpy() in the 'alloc_new' block would copy 0 bytes" and (2) "When shrinking an object while forcing a new alignment, ... the memcpy() used the old size ('orig_size ?: ks'), leading to an out-of-bounds write." The patch fixes these by moving the old size calculation before the early jump and using `min(new_size, (size_t)(orig_size ?: ks))` to bound the copy length, and similarly using `min(size, ksize(p))` in kvrealloc.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix krealloc behavior to not migrate to a different node when __GFP_THISNODE is set and the new size is smaller, as the existing allocation should be preserved.
intent_record.what: Removed a conditional block in __do_krealloc that forced a new allocation when __GFP_THISNODE was set and the current page's node did not match the requested node, even if the new size was smaller than the current allocation.
intent_record.how: Previously, when __GFP_THISNODE was set and the node mismatch occurred, the function would jump to alloc_new, causing a reallocation regardless of size. After removal, the function proceeds to subsequent checks (e.g., kfence) and will typically return the existing pointer if the new size is not larger, thus avoiding unnecessary node migration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix krealloc to honor __GFP_THISNODE flag by reallocating on the requested node even when the new size is not larger.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional block before the size-based reallocation check that forces reallocation if __GFP_THISNODE is set and the current object is not on the requested NUMA node.
intent_record.how: When __GFP_THISNODE is specified, the kernel now ensures that the reallocated object resides on the specified node by allocating a new object if the existing one is on a different node, regardless of whether the new size is smaller or equal.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential buffer overflow in krealloc when shrinking allocation by limiting the copy size to the minimum of new size and old size.
intent_record.what: Changed the third argument to memcpy in __do_krealloc from `orig_size ?: ks` to `min(new_size, (size_t)(orig_size ?: ks))`.
intent_record.how: Ensures that when krealloc shrinks an allocation, the memory copy does not exceed the new buffer size, preventing a buffer overflow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential buffer over-copy in kvrealloc by limiting memcpy to min(size, ksize(p)) when reallocating to a smaller size.
intent_record.what: Changed the memcpy size argument from ksize(p) to min(size, ksize(p)) in kvrealloc_node_align_noprof.
intent_record.how: Limits the number of bytes copied from the old allocation to the new allocation to the minimum of the requested new size and the actual old allocation size, preventing copying extra bytes when the new size is smaller.

relevance_review.reason: Group 0's changes focus on honoring __GFP_THISNODE to prevent node migration, which is a functional enhancement unrelated to the root cause of uninitialized old size variables and improper memcpy length in fallback paths.
The group directly addresses the root cause by bounding the memcpy copy length to the minimum of the new and old sizes in krealloc and kvrealloc, preventing over-copy when shrinking allocation.

In the kvrealloc fallback path, the memcpy copy length uses 'ksize(p)' (the old size) without bounding to the new allocation size, causing an out-of-bounds write when shrinking the allocation.
